function: Excluded (above_phy): multi-agent RL learns RIS-subarray handover and user association (pp. 20-22); the learned imputation/forecasting predicts user-tracking and blockage information, not channel, beams, or detection.
notes: p. 20: "formulate the handover and user association problem of an RIS-assisted THz indoor network serving XR users". p. 22: "The action of each agent is to perform a handover decision or to maintain the currently active link" (binary action; the beam is then pointed at the tracked user, not learned). p. 13: "these predictions are not predicting the proper LoS and NLoS values"; the learned imputation (NAOMI-style RNN) and adversarial transformer forecast sensing parameters (AoA, AoD, ToA of users and blockers) as inputs to the handover agent. pp. 9-12 and 28: the sensing parameters themselves come from a non-learned tensor decomposition (ALS, Appendix A), with a CRLB. Even if the sensing forecast were counted as physical layer, it is user tracking and blockage forecasting, outside the seven areas (function would also exclude). Quantitative simulation results are reported (pp. 25-27), so results does not apply. The PDF is arXiv 2305.00135v1, titled Joint Sensing, Communication, and AI: A Trifecta for Resilient THz User Experiences, which matches the title and authors of the TWC paper.
